title: Ethical Hacking Workshop
description: A beginner-friendly live workshop on what ethical hacking really is. Learn how security professionals find weaknesses before criminals do — legally and responsibly. The perfect first step into cybersecurity.
syllabus:
What ethical hacking really is (and is not)
Setting up Kali Linux safely in a VM
Reconnaissance: information gathering basics
Scanning networks with Nmap
Common web vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10 intro)
Career roadmap: becoming an ethical hacker

title: Web Security Basics
description: Websites are attacked every day. In this hands-on workshop you will see the most common web attacks explained simply, and learn the basic defenses every developer and site owner should know.
syllabus:
How the web works: requests, responses, sessions
SQL Injection — what it is and how to prevent it
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) explained with demos
Broken authentication & weak passwords
HTTPS, security headers and safe coding habits
Free tools to test your own website safely

title: Linux for Hackers
description: Almost every cybersecurity professional works on Linux. This workshop takes you from zero to comfortable with the Linux terminal — the single most useful skill for a security career.
syllabus:
Why hackers and professionals choose Linux
Installing Linux / using it without disturbing Windows
Terminal basics: files, folders, permissions
Essential commands: grep, find, ssh, curl
Package management and basic scripting
Practice roadmap after the workshop

title: Networking Fundamentals
description: You cannot secure what you do not understand. Learn how data travels across networks, what IP addresses and ports really mean, and how attackers abuse weak network setups — explained in plain language.
syllabus:
IP addresses, subnets and ports — simply explained
TCP vs UDP, DNS and HTTP in plain words
How Wi-Fi and routers work (and their weak points)
Reading network traffic with Wireshark basics
Common network attacks and simple defenses
What to learn next: CCNA-style roadmap
